$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

architect.rationale: One app, two small sequential slices in orchestra/mobile. Not a diamond: both slices touch package.json (s1 edits it; the s2 prebuild rewrites its scripts and must restore them), and the s2 manifest proof must run on the s1 dependency tree. Real edge s1 -> s2. orchestra is a git repo, so each slice gets a worktree branch. Risk: s1 high, because it changes native module versions (expo, expo-router, @expo/ui, expo-network). Jest mocks native code, so the tests cannot see a native break; only the owner device run sees it. s2 high, because it touches eas.json (native-mobile rule) and records a security trade-off (cleartext in release builds) whose wording the reviewer must check against the code. DECISIONS. (1) Cleartext: KEEP it app-wide and document it as a decided trade-off covering preview AND production builds. An Android network security config can only list domains, not IP ranges or CIDRs, and the hosts are arbitrary LAN or Tailscale IPs. Any config that works is base-config cleartextPermitted=true, which is today with more files. The Noise channel carries the security, and the app opens no other connection (orchestra/CLAUDE.md:159-161). The owner approves one added sentence. (2) expo-updates: NOT now. It makes the app contact u.expo.dev at launch, which breaks the rule that the app opens no other connection and the no-phone-home stance. Its updates.url needs the projectId, which only the owner eas init creates. Under the fingerprint policy, adding it later means one more build, which for a sideloaded preview APK is one more owner build. Revisit before the Play production track. The eas.json channels stay, inert. (3) Version drift: FIX it in s1 with npx expo install --fix, within SDK 57, so the first EAS build matches what EAS and expo-doctor expect. (4) versionCode: ADD autoIncrement true to build.preview. With appVersionSource remote and no autoIncrement, preview reuses the remote code and two APKs cannot be told apart. The remote counter is per platform, not per profile, so it is shared with production. That is harmless, because Play needs codes to rise, not to be contiguous. (5) Verification: s2 runs prebuild --no-install --clean in the worktree, greps the generated manifest (cleartext, RECORD_AUDIO remove, INTERNET) and the gradle targetSdk fallback (36 or higher), then deletes android/ and restores package.json. The final merged manifest is proven only by the owner device pairing over ws with the EAS APK. (6) Docs: a build-and-install section in mobile/README.md (s2). (7) No EAS CI workflow: it needs an EXPO_TOKEN secret, which is credential handling agents may not do. It spends EAS build quota for one owner device, and test.yml already runs tsc and jest. Revisit with the Play tracks or R1.

findings.issue: The README compresses architect.owner_steps and drops step 4 (eas whoami, to confirm the njcurtis3 account) and step 6's 'git diff app.json, expect only owner and extra.eas.projectId' before 'git commit -am'. Run from mobile/, -am stages every modified tracked file in the whole orchestra repo, so any stray local edit, such as a package.json left rewritten by a local prebuild, would be swept into the EAS link commit. Ignored files (ROADMAP.md, /android, *.jks) are not at risk. Suggested fix: add 'eas whoami' and 'git diff' lines, or use 'git commit app.json -m'.

The full permission list is CAMERA, INTERNET, POST_NOTIFICATIONS, READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdk 32), RECORD_AUDIO (remove), SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, VIBRATE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdk 32). INTERNET and VIBRATE are normal permissions, and SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW shows under Special app access, not the Permissions list. So D1 ('only Camera and Notifications') holds on Android 13+, but on an Android 12 or older device the storage permissions would appear as Files and media. They come from the Expo prebuild template, and SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is unneeded in a release build. Blocking them means changing app.json blockedPermissions, which is out of scope for s2 (not_doing). Candidate follow-up.
